10. WARNING ENZYME-BEFORE-DILUENT: An enzyme was added before the water: rt
   line 54:  p300.dispense(vol, dest)
   reached through: run:62 > transfer_with_tip:54
   At line 54 the robot put rt into tube B1 in slot 2. Take tube B1 in slot 2: at that
   moment it held only 52.8 ul, all of it neat buffer, and the water came afterwards, at
   line 54, to make the 118.8 ul of water or buffer the reaction is built on. An enzyme is
   shipped in 50% glycerol and is meant to be the last thing into a reaction, after the
   water and the buffer have brought the well to the right dilution. Dropped into neat
   buffer or a dry well it meets many times the salt it should: a restriction enzyme then
   cuts at the wrong places (star activity) and a polymerase starts on mis-primed template.
   Affected: tube B1 in slot 2.
   Fix: Reorder the additions to tube B1 in slot 2: water and buffer first, then the sample,
   then rt last. Or make a master mix of water, buffer and enzyme in one tube, mix it, and
   hand it out.
   Source: Thermo Fisher: restriction enzyme key considerations (the enzyme is the final
   component)
           https://www.thermofisher.com/us/en/home/life-science/cloning/cloning-learning-center/invitrogen-school-of-molecular-biology/molecular-cloning/restriction-enzymes/restriction-enzyme-key-considerations.html
   Source: Promega: restriction enzyme resource (add the enzyme last; glycerol and star
   activity)
           https://www.promega.com/resources/guides/nucleic-acid-analysis/restriction-enzyme-resource/
   Source: NEB: Q5 High-Fidelity PCR kit manual (add the polymerase last)
           https://www.neb.com/-/media/nebus/files/manuals/manuale0555.pdf
   Source: Qiagen: critical factors for successful real-time PCR (order of addition)
           https://www.gene-quantification.de/qiagen-qpcr-sample-assay-tech-guide-2010.pdf
   [7a314924f530]

13. NOTE NO-NEGATIVE-CONTROL: No no-template control: 24 wells of dntp with a sample
   line 94:  p300.dispense(12.0, dst_plate[r_well])
   At line 94 the robot starts putting dntp into NEST 96 Well Plate 100 µL PCR Full Skirt
   (slot 4), and 24 wells end holding it together with a sample. No well on this plate holds
   the mix without a sample, so there is no no-template control. If a reagent is
   contaminated, or the primers pair with each other, every well gives a signal and nothing
   on the plate can tell that from a real one. Wells: wells A1, A2, A3, B1, B2, B3, C1, C2
   and 16 more in slot 4.
   Affected: wells A1, A2, A3, B1, B2, B3, C1, C2 and 16 more in slot 4.
   Fix: Add one well (three for qPCR) with 1 ul of dntp and 8 ul of water in place of the
   template, and tell the plate map where it is.

           https://gene-quantification.com/miqe-bustin-et-al-clin-chem-2009.pdf

findings.title: An enzyme was added before the water: rt
findings.explanation: At line 54 the robot put rt into tube B1 in slot 2. Take tube B1 in slot 2: at that moment it held only 52.8 ul, all of it neat buffer, and the water came afterwards, at line 54, to make the 118.8 ul of water or buffer the reaction is built on. An enzyme is shipped in 50% glycerol and is meant to be the last thing into a reaction, after the water and the buffer have brought the well to the right dilution. Dropped into neat buffer or a dry well it meets many times the salt it should: a restriction enzyme then cuts at the wrong places (star activity) and a polymerase starts on mis-primed template.
findings.fix: Reorder the additions to tube B1 in slot 2: water and buffer first, then the sample, then rt last. Or make a master mix of water, buffer and enzyme in one tube, mix it, and hand it out.

findings.title: Mixing too weak to stir tube B1 in slot 2: 3 × 33 ul in 158.4 ul
findings.explanation: At line 56 the tip mixes tube B1 in slot 2 with 3 strokes of 33 ul in a well holding 158.4 ul. 3 strokes of 33 ul move 0.62 of the well in all; it takes about 2 wells' worth of strokes to mix (the mixing work). Integra draws over 80% of the well five times; three mixes gave 11.8% CV where twenty gave 1.7%. What the well holds is not at the concentration you calculated, and in a dilution series every later step inherits the error.
findings.fix: Mix the well with about 80% of its volume (126.7 ul) at least 5 times: `mix(5, 126.7, well)`. A stroke of the whole well draws air; use no more than 90%.

findings.title: No no-template control: 24 wells of dntp with a sample
findings.explanation: At line 94 the robot starts putting dntp into NEST 96 Well Plate 100 µL PCR Full Skirt (slot 4), and 24 wells end holding it together with a sample. No well on this plate holds the mix without a sample, so there is no no-template control. If a reagent is contaminated, or the primers pair with each other, every well gives a signal and nothing on the plate can tell that from a real one. Wells: wells A1, A2, A3, B1, B2, B3, C1, C2 and 16 more in slot 4.
findings.fix: Add one well (three for qPCR) with 1 ul of dntp and 8 ul of water in place of the template, and tell the plate map where it is.
